New UN Map Depicts Arunachal Pradesh and Aksai Chin as Territories Caught Between Indian and Chinese Lines

2026-09-07 The Hindu UN, Correct the Map, Arunachal Pradesh, Aksai Chin, India, China, territorial dispute, cartographic representation, Mercator, Equal Earth, borders
Read the source article

Quick summary

A new UN world map published following the "Correct the Map" resolution depicts Arunachal Pradesh and Aksai Chin as territories between Indian and Chinese claim lines, prompting India's MEA to reiterate that any inaccurate depiction of its sovereign territory is unacceptable.

Key takeaways

  • The UN map published July 1, 2026 shows Arunachal Pradesh's southern border with Assam as the "Chinese Line" and its northern border with Tibet as the "Indian Line"
  • Aksai Chin's eastern borders are labeled "Indian Line" while a "Chinese line" demarcates Ladakh from Aksai Chin
  • India claims Aksai Chin as part of Ladakh, but the map shows separate Indian and Chinese claim lines without explanatory notes
  • The map depicts Jammu and Kashmir with a dotted Line of Control, clarified as an India-Pakistan agreement with final status not yet agreed
  • India's MEA reiterated that the vote supported the principle of equal-area representation, not endorsement of any specific map or boundary depiction
  • The map appears to favor India on the Kalapani-Lipulekh-Limpiyadhura border dispute with Nepal, reflecting Indian control
